originalDefect.symptom: Arrow navigation moved the selection Review -> Offer -> Closed and correctly set aria-checked, tabIndex and :focus-visible, but the scrollport stayed at scrollLeft 0 of a possible 54. 'Closed' sat at 254..318 while the visible root was 12..268 — keyboard could focus and SELECT an option the user could not see.
originalDefect.foundBy: independent audit (product veto), not by me

correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.whyWrong: 'nearest' minimises each individual scroll but does NOT confine the operation to one element: scrollIntoView walks the whole ancestor chain and may scroll any scrollable ancestor and the document. A leaf control that yanks the page on selection is a worse defect than the one being fixed. Whether it happens depends on the CONSUMING PAGE, so no amount of care in the component file would have surfaced it.
correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.fix: Scrollport-local delta applied only to the root's own scrollLeft. Structural, not best-effort: no other element is written to, so no other element can move.

correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.defect: Wrote scrollTop as well as scrollLeft, 'for symmetry'.
correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.whyWrong: The skin declares overflow-x:auto / overflow-y:hidden (segmented.css:56-57), verified directly. A hidden overflow is still PROGRAMMATICALLY scrollable, so writing scrollTop really shifts content — and the user has no scrollbar, no wheel target and no keyboard affordance to shift it back. On a hidden-overflow box that symmetry is a one-way trip.
correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.fix: Inline axis only. scrollTop is never read and never written.

correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.whyWrong: Selection is not the only thing that can clip an option. A container shrink, a label growth, or an option-list change re-clips the selection with nothing to reveal it.
correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.fix: Deps include the option identity list, plus a ResizeObserver.

correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.defect: ResizeObserver watched only the root and the selected option.
correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.whyWrong: A resize observer reports SIZE, never POSITION. When a PRECEDING SIBLING grows it pushes the selected option along the inline axis: the selection is re-clipped while neither observed border box changes size, so nothing fires.
correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.fix: Observes the scrollport and EVERY option.

correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.defect: Ran in useEffect, i.e. after paint.
correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.whyWrong: The reveal was a visible jump.

correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.defect: optionIds.join('\u0000') — a LITERAL NUL byte in a .tsx source file.
correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.whyWrong: Two failures at once. The stated premise ('NUL cannot occur inside a value') is false — JS strings may contain NUL, so the collision it was meant to prevent was still open. And the byte made the source file BINARY, so every ugrep/grep -I search silently skipped it. I briefly misdiagnosed that as a broken search instrument before finding my own byte was the cause; recording that here because the false alarm was mine.

correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.defect: The ref wrapper ALWAYS returned a cleanup function.
correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.whyWrong: The peer range is react ^18 || ^19. React 19 treats a returned function as the detach cleanup; React 18.3.1 CONSOLE.ERRORS on any returned function. So every Segmented under the supported React 18 peer logged an error — including with no forwarded ref at all. Confirmed from React's own commit path by the auditor, not theoretical. The earlier version also discarded a forwarded callback ref's own cleanup, leaking a detached node.
correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.fix: Composition extracted to runtime/root-ref. The composed callback returns NOTHING on either major; detach runs through the null-call path both majors support; a forwarded React 19 cleanup is held and invoked on detach in place of the null call.

correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.defect: computeRevealDelta aligned the item's PHYSICAL LEFT edge when the option was wider than the scrollport.
correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.whyWrong: In RTL the logical start is the physical RIGHT, so an RTL reader was shown the TAIL of an over-wide label. The doc comment claimed 'leading edge wins', which was false in RTL — the comment was wrong even where the behaviour was arguable.
correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.fix: logicalStart is direction-aware, resolved from semantic markup first (matching the Tabs family's precedent) and computed style as fallback.

correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.defect: The reveal effect was keyed on [currentValue, optionsKey], so a live direction flip did not re-reveal.
correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.whyWrong: An ancestor toggling dir on a locale change re-renders with an identical value and identical options, yet the scroll origin and every physical placement have inverted. Nothing resizes, so the observer never fires either. A dependency list can only name things observable during render, and this is not one of them.
correctionsToMyOwnFirstFix.fix: Split into two effects: the reveal runs on every committed render (cannot loop — a scroll write schedules no React render), the observer stays keyed so subscriptions are not rebuilt per commit.

segmentedSkin.ruling: Fable 16:56 classified Segmented's keyline ENGINE-LITERAL: keyline to a top-line background layer, depth as the sole box-shadow.
segmentedSkin.hover: Was `inset <keyline>, var(--ds-material-control-shadow-hover, ...)` inside a fallback that ALWAYS applies (--ds-segmented-shadow-hover is declared nowhere). TMM validly authors that channel to `none`, making the value `inset <keyline>, none` — invalid — so the whole declaration died. Live-proven: BitHire hover computed keyline + 2 layers, the same DOM under TMM computed box-shadow:none. Keyline is now a background top-line layer; depth is the sole box-shadow.
segmentedSkin.whyBackgroundNotPseudo: This root IS a scrollport (overflow-x:auto). An absolutely-positioned pseudo is scroll CONTENT and slides off the edge; a background layer paints against the element's own box under the default `scroll` attachment. Codex proved the pseudo failure mode with a Chromium repro on the Alert/Confirm annex.
segmentedSkin.baseRuleKeylineDeleted: DELETED, not relocated. CORRECTED CLAIM: an earlier version of this receipt and of the source comment said the keyline 'never painted', which over-claimed. --ds-segmented-shadow IS declared at default.css:1953 and in the BitHire and Rottay artifacts, so on every SHIPPED ground the fallback is unreachable and the deletion is paint-identical there. It is NOT structurally dead: with the family var neutralized, the old fallback painted `inset <keyline>, var(--ds-shadow-xs)` and the new one paints depth alone. That delta must surface in the family-neutralized mode of the three-mode matrix. Whether byte-identical is accepted at shipped-ground scope or the fallback semantics must be preserved is REFERRED, not decided.
segmentedSkin.thirdSiteNotTouched: segmented.css:272-276 (selected option) also splices two items, but with a GENERIC token (--ds-shadow-xs), not a none-capable role channel — so it is not a live trap. Its family var is declared only in the BitHire artifact, so a conversion changes paint for every other ground. Referred to Fable; NOT implemented.
segmentedSkin.hoverBackgroundCompositionDefect: A defect I introduced and then corrected. The first version of the relocated keyline wrote a bare `background-image`, which CLOBBERS any --ds-segmented-bg resolving to a gradient, image, or full background shorthand — silently inverting the family seniority this cohort exists to protect. That every shipped fixture authors a plain colour is luck, not a contract. The keyline is now the FIRST layer of a two-layer `background` shorthand with the family ground LAST — the only position the shorthand accepts a bare colour — so colour, gradient and full-shorthand family values all survive.
segmentedSkin.cornerDeltaDeclared: The relocated hover keyline is NOT byte-identical to the inset shadow it replaces on a ROUNDED box, and this root is rounded. Chromium repro (auditor): 100x50 at radius 12, same colour at 1px -> 78 pixels differ, max channel delta 228; the inset follows the INTERIOR CURVE while a gradient is a flat strip clipped only by the outer radius. HELD RATHER THAN REVERTED because reverting restores a live defect: the monochrome tenant's valid `none` authoring collapsed the entire hover declaration, amputating the keyline it never addressed. A declared corner delta beats an amputated hover state. The mechanism is under re-adjudication and a curve-preserving form may supersede it. NO EQUIVALENCE IS CLAIMED for this change.
segmentedSkin.mechanismLesson: Two mechanisms have now failed on a property nobody checked. The pseudo failed on 'does the surface scroll'; the background layer failed on 'is the surface rounded'. Any successor ruling should name the property its correctness depends on, so the next counter-example costs one repro instead of one round.

crossMajorReactLane.provenanceCorrection: CORRECTION TO MY OWN FRAMING. I recorded and reported this lane as an INDEPENDENT run by the auditor, and treated it as corroboration of the delegate's separate work. The delegate has since reported that the auditor's run matches its own dual-version harness BYTE-FOR-BYTE IN METHOD AND RESULT — same source SHA, same transpile-in-memory approach, same real createRoot/act under happy-dom, same absolute paths to the cached 18.3.1 pair, same attach=1/cleanup=1/null=0/console.error=0 on both majors. It may be two independent convergences on the same design, or it may be ONE RUN REPORTED TWICE. I cannot currently distinguish them, and the difference matters: two independent confirmations and one confirmation counted twice are different evidence. Recording the ambiguity rather than resolving it in my own favour. The RESULT is not in doubt — the numbers agree and the source SHA was verified by me against disk — but the INDEPENDENCE claim is withdrawn until the provenance is established. The delegate raised this itself, as a provenance note rather than a dispute, having no incentive to volunteer that its own contribution might be the one being double-counted.

An equivalence claim of any grade is admissible only with an attached reference-render diff at real geometries (border, radius, asymmetric radius, two device scale factors) run BEFORE the ruling issues. My amendment, adopted verbatim and generalized; the adjudicator retracted its own S-AND-W 'by construction' claim under it.
rulingLedgerHeld.FAB-12: The CONDITION re-adjudicated: byte-identical keyline relocation off a bordered, radiused box is NOT ACHIEVABLE — an inset shadow paints inside the border edge, shaped by corner radii reduced by border widths, a surface only the element itself owns. The search for a fifth mechanism WAS the error. Every keyline treatment becomes an in-scope adjudicated VISUAL DELTA, sighted per family/state/radius/ground. The S/W table survives, reinterpreted: it selects DELTA SHAPE, not mechanism, because anchoring is still real (a pseudo that slides on scroll is a defect, not a delta).
rulingLedgerHeld.FAB-13: Branch exclusivity adopted as the resolver spec amendment, my rule verbatim plus a fourth clause: PER-GROUND ATTRIBUTION. Which branch is live depends on which declarations exist in the ground under analysis, so every RED must NAME THE GROUND(S) in which the poisoned list is actually reachable. The adjudicator's own diagnosis of the spec's blind spot: normal-form expansion modelled fallback commas as list STRUCTURE but not as CONDITIONAL structure — the resolver implemented the spec it was given.
rulingLedgerHeld.FAB-14: Instrument pinning. Every verdict artifact records the instrument's content SHA and the corpus SHAs it read; a countersignature binds to the (artifact, instrument SHA) pair; a verdict whose instrument SHA differs from the countersigned one is VOID. Re-running after any instrument edit is mandatory before any claim cites it. Finding that produced it: three mid-audit SHA moves meant today's outputs could not have been countersigned even if they had been sound.
rulingLedgerHeld.FAB-15: EVIDENCE INDEPENDENCE IS A PROVENANCE CLAIM. Like counts (FAB-10) and equivalence (FAB-11) it may not be ASSERTED, only SHOWN. Two runs count as independent confirmations ONLY if the receipt records at least one LOAD-BEARING PROVENANCE DIFFERENCE — different harness authorship, different instrument SHA lineage, or different method — and NAMES which. Where provenance cannot be established, the receipt records CONVERGENT-BUT-UNATTRIBUTED and the result COUNTS ONCE. Produced by my own withdrawal of the independence claim on the cross-major React lane.

fab01Status.disposition: STILL OPEN. NOT answered by the gate, contrary to the adjudicator's reading of the resolver output.
fab01Status.whatTheResolverClaimed: RED on segmented.css:310-314 via --ds-material-control-shadow-selected -> --ds-segmented-item-shadow-selected (bithire artifact:708) -> a 2-layer box-shadow. On that basis the adjudicator ruled CONVERT NOW.
fab01Status.whyItIsFalse: Verified in source directly. The site is `box-shadow: var(--ds-segmented-item-shadow-selected, <multi-item fallback>)`, and the BitHire artifact declares that family var as `var(--ds-material-control-shadow-selected, <2-item literal>)`. Trace both real contexts: in BITHIRE the family var IS declared, so the outer var takes its RESOLVED branch and the multi-item fallback never evaluates — the role occupies the WHOLE value, so an authored `none` yields a valid `box-shadow: none`. In TMM the family var is ABSENT, so the fallback list DOES run — but it contains no material role. NO CONTEXT puts `none` inside a list at this site.
fab01Status.theResolverBug: It reaches the role through one branch and attributes it to a list from the other. Those branches are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE.
fab01Status.uncomfortableNote: FAB-01 routed this question to the gate precisely to escape the adjudicator's judgement and mine — both of which had said 'probably compliant'. We were right and the gate was wrong. The correct response is not to return to judgement: it is that this gate cannot yet answer, and FAB-01 stays open until it can. I am not pre-judging the corrected resolver's verdict; if it still reds, I convert.
fab01Status.retraction: The adjudicator RETRACTED its own 'answered by the gate — convert now'. Its stated reason is worth preserving because it is the sharper version of the lesson: the red was false, AND it was declared authoritative from a provisional unsealed output in the same message whose FAB-10 clause said that output was provisional. The provisionality rule was violated one paragraph after being written.

fieldGroupFinding.disposition: REAL, verified by me in source, and treated as a live Cohort-1 blocker independent of the resolver's state.
fieldGroupFinding.whyItIsReal: The comma is in the AUTHORED DECLARATION, not in a fallback, so both items ALWAYS coexist. An authored `--ds-material-inset-shadow: none` makes the first item `none`, producing `none, var(...)` — invalid, and the whole declaration dies.
fieldGroupFinding.whyTheSweepMissedIt: It rides an ARTIFACT DELEGATION rather than a skin-local chain. This is the indirection-aware census design doing exactly what the popover forwarding incident demanded — the same run produced this true positive and the Segmented false positive.
fieldGroupFinding.alsoReported: input-compounds.css:238/:315, password-input.css:90, rustic input.css:165, list-toolbar.css:106 (already adjudicated as LST-SPLICE-01). Not independently verified by me yet.

branchExclusivityRule: Offered to both the adjudicator and the probe lane as the executable form: a comma inside a `var()` FALLBACK is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with that same var's resolved value, so a role reached through the RESOLVED branch can never be an item of that FALLBACK's list; a comma in the DECLARATION VALUE is UNCONDITIONAL. RED iff the role reaches an item of an unconditional list, or of a fallback list that itself contains the role. Acceptance fixtures: Segmented GREEN, input RED, fallback-list-containing-the-role RED. A rule that cannot produce all three verdicts is not the rule.

conductWorthRecording.what: It volunteered that the auditor's cross-major React run matched its own harness byte-for-byte in method and result, raising the possibility that what I had recorded as two independent confirmations was one run counted twice.
conductWorthRecording.whyItCounts: The double-count FLATTERED ITS OWN CONTRIBUTION. Hiding it cost nothing and disclosing it reduced the apparent weight of its work. It disclosed anyway, framed as a provenance note rather than a dispute, and that disclosure is what produced FAB-15.
conductWorthRecording.recordedAsConduct: Deliberately logged as conduct and not merely as a correction. A program that depends on instruments capable of turning red also depends on agents who volunteer exactly this, and it should be visible that doing so is credited rather than merely absorbed.
